speaker: NARRATOR
text: August 2nd, 216 BC. Southern Italy. The Roman Republic has gathered the biggest army in its entire history. Eight legions. Plus allies. Somewhere around eighty thousand men.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: We are SO going to win this.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Across the field stands a Carthaginian general with a much smaller army, a lot of mercenaries who don't speak the same language… and only one working eye.

speaker: HANNIBAL
text: Perfect.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: By sunset, the Roman army will be gone. Not defeated. Gone.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: …Wait, what?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: To understand Cannae, you need to know about the two superpowers of the western Mediterranean. Rome: farmers, soldiers, and very, very stubborn. And Carthage: a rich trading empire in North Africa, with the best navy around and enough money to hire anyone it needed.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: They had already fought one massive war over Sicily. It lasted twenty-three years, and Carthage lost.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: Yay!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: One of the Carthaginian generals in that war was a man named Hamilcar Barca. And Hamilcar did not handle losing well.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: According to the story, he took his nine-year-old son to an altar and made him swear that he would never be a friend to Rome.

speaker: HANNIBAL
text: I promise, Father.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: That boy's name… was Hannibal.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: Oh no.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Years later, Hannibal is grown up, in command of Carthage's army in Spain, and ready to keep his promise. In 218 BC, war breaks out again. Rome expects to fight in Spain, or in Africa. Normal places.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Hannibal has a different idea. He will march overland… through the Pyrenees… across southern France… and over the Alps. In the autumn. With war elephants.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: Elephants? In the MOUNTAINS?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: It was brutal. Snow, landslides, and local tribes rolling rocks onto his men. Hannibal lost a huge part of his army on the way. But in the end, he did it. A Carthaginian army had appeared in northern Italy, out of nowhere.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: That's… that's cheating!

speaker: HANNIBAL
text: It's called planning.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Rome sends an army to deal with him. At the River Trebia, in December, Hannibal tricks the Romans into wading through an icy river before breakfast, then ambushes them.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: S-s-so c-cold…

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The next year Rome tries again. At Lake Trasimene, Hannibal hides his entire army in the hills above a foggy lakeshore… and waits. The Roman army marches straight into the trap. The Roman commander, the consul Flaminius, is killed.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Oh, and somewhere along the way, Hannibal spent days marching through flooded marshes, caught an infection, and lost the sight in one eye. It did not slow him down at all.

speaker: HANNIBAL
text: I only need one eye to watch Romans run.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: After two disasters, Rome tries something new. They give power to an old senator named Quintus Fabius Maximus. And Fabius has a very clever plan.

speaker: ELDER
text: We will not fight him.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: …That's the plan?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Fabius follows Hannibal around Italy, cuts his supplies, picks off small groups… but refuses to fight a big battle. Hannibal is in enemy land, far from home. Time is on Rome's side.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: It was smart. And the Romans absolutely hated it. They gave Fabius a nickname: Cunctator. "The Delayer." It was not a compliment.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: So for 216 BC, Rome elects two new consuls, Lucius Aemilius Paullus and Gaius Terentius Varro, and gives them the biggest army it has ever raised. The goal: find Hannibal, and crush him.

speaker: VARRO
text: No more waiting! No more delaying! We attack!

speaker: SOBIUS
text: Yeah! …Wait, why am I in the front row?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The two armies meet near a small town called Cannae, in southern Italy, beside the River Aufidus. The two consuls take turns commanding, one day each. On August 2nd, it's Varro's turn.

speaker: VARRO
text: Today is my day.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Varro's plan is simple. He packs his infantry into a deep, heavy block in the middle, and plans to smash straight through the Carthaginian center like a battering ram.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: I can't… move… my arms…

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Hannibal looks at this, and does something very strange. He puts his weakest troops, Gauls and Spaniards, in the center, and pushes them forward into a bulge, curving out towards the Romans.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Behind them, on both sides, out of sight, he places his best soldiers: veteran African infantry. And on the wings, his cavalry. Heavy horsemen on one side, fast Numidian riders on the other.

speaker: HANNIBAL
text: Let them come.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: One more thing. Ancient writers say the wind that day blew hot and dusty… straight into the Romans' faces.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: Why is it always ME?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The battle begins. The giant Roman block charges into Hannibal's center, and at first, it works. The Gauls and Spaniards are pushed back. Step by step. The bulge flattens… then caves inward.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: They're running! We're winning!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The Romans push deeper and deeper into the gap. More and more of them crowd into the middle.

speaker: HANNIBAL
text: Now.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: On both sides, the African veterans turn inward and slam into the Roman flanks. Meanwhile, Hannibal's heavy cavalry has already crushed the Roman horsemen by the river. Instead of chasing them, they ride all the way around, behind the Roman army… help the Numidians drive off the allied cavalry… and then charge into the Roman rear.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: Uh… guys? Why are there Carthaginians… behind us?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The Roman army is completely surrounded. So tightly packed, most soldiers can't even raise their swords. The men in the middle can't see what's happening, and they can't escape.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: By the end of the day, the Roman army had been destroyed. Polybius says around seventy thousand were killed. Livy gives a smaller number, about forty-eight thousand. Either way, it was one of the bloodiest single days of battle in all of history.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The consul Paullus died on the field. Varro escaped. Hannibal lost somewhere between six and eight thousand men.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Hannibal's brother sailed home to Carthage with the news. According to Livy, he poured a pile of gold rings onto the floor of the senate. Rings taken from dead Roman nobles.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: That's… so rude.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Everyone expected Rome to surrender. One of Hannibal's cavalry commanders, Maharbal, begged him to march on Rome right away.

speaker: ELDER
text: You know how to win a victory, Hannibal. But you do not know how to use one.

speaker: HANNIBAL
text: …I'll think about it.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Hannibal didn't march on Rome. And Rome… simply refused to give up. No peace talks. They raised new legions. They even armed slaves. And they went back to the strategy everyone had hated: the Delayer's strategy.

speaker: ELDER
text: Told you.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Hannibal stayed in Italy for another thirteen years. He was never defeated there. But he never took Rome, either. In the end, Rome took the war to Africa, and in 202 BC, Hannibal was finally beaten at the Battle of Zama.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: But Cannae was never forgotten. For more than two thousand years, generals have studied it as the perfect example of surrounding and destroying a bigger army. Hannibal won the battle of the century… and still lost the war.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: So… we lost the battle… but we won the war?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Yes.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: So I can stop crying?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Next episode: the Battle of Kadesh, where two kings both claimed they won… and carved it in stone.

speaker: SOBIUS
text: More wars?!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Subscribe to Spears & Tears, so you don't miss it.
